methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: After severe 76% electricity price hikes due to AI data centers, Virginia requires firms to pay for all dedicated upstream electrical infrastructure — state regulators crack down, governor says move will save civilians ‘hundreds of millions of dollars’ - Tom's Hardware
signals.signal_reading: Massive electricity price hikes from concentrated NoVA data centers create infrastructure costs that deepen the metro advantage—regions with AI infrastructure can absorb costs and attract investment, while regions without face barriers to entry and economic spillover without capability building.

signals.title: Roanoke College launches WorkAI Lab to prepare leaders for new era of technology - Roanoke College
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke College's WorkAI Lab represents intentional capability-building outside metro hubs, signaling potential for distributed deep literacy if the institution can create peer networks that spread AI fluency beyond campus into Southwest Virginia's transitioning economy.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free community-led AI workshops in Hampton Roads demonstrate grassroots knowledge distribution outside traditional tech corridors, suggesting Bottom-up capability building that could enable broad fluency if sustained beyond individual initiatives into institutional support.

signals.title: Google to invest millions for Virginia workforce development amid data center growth - WRIC ABC 8News
signals.signal_reading: Google's workforce development investment tied to data center growth signals platform-driven shallow adoption—corporate training for data center operations creates jobs but not deep AI capability, reinforcing Richmond as service provider rather than innovation center.

signals.title: IT Department Lays Out AI Policy for Norfolk Classrooms - GovTech
signals.signal_reading: Norfolk's AI policy for classrooms represents administrative adoption of platform tools rather than fundamental literacy building—policy frameworks for using AI tools create shallow distributed access without the deep capability needed for local innovation or economic leadership.
